style: Two looks, as in the game's stills. images.title: Lanterns under five dark fingers
images.prompt: Photographic macro miniature diorama, tilt-shift, shallow depth of field, fine dust in the lit air. A vertical wall of deep umber tree bark seen straight on, filling the whole frame edge to edge like a cliff. Across the lower half clings a tiny city of round carved dwellings with bark-chip shutters, dozens of orange glow-lichen lanterns lit, amber sap beading in the grooves, patches of sage and lime lichen. The upper half of the bark lies in a flat soft blue-black cast shadow whose lower edge is shaped into five long tapering lobes pointing down, a shadow only, painted by light on the bark surface, its lowest tip just reaching the highest lantern. In a strip of gold light, right of centre, a small kite made of one sage-green leaf hangs on a silk thread. The upper third is calm shadowed bark with nothing on it, left empty for a title. One low warm light from below left. Nothing in front of the bark: no hand, no fingers, no skin, no people, no text, no lettering, no watermark, no logo

A large old deciduous tree with grey-brown bark stands on a mown green lawn, its whole trunk in the left third of the frame, a white picket fence behind it, blue sky. Sunlight lies on the bark where the hand had rested. Nothing on the bark can be made out at this distance: it is just a tree. Grass green, sky blue, white fence, bark umber. images.title: The Flake
images.prompt: Photographic macro miniature diorama, tilt-shift, shallow depth of field, fine dust in the lit air. A vertical wall of rough umber tree bark seen straight on. On the left half a tiny city of round carved dwellings with round doors and bark-chip shutters clings to the bark ridges, its lanterns unlit. At the middle of the frame the city and the bark stop at a clean new edge, and the right half is a broad bare scar of pale smooth fresh inner wood, empty and quiet, where a plate of bark has come away. Nothing is falling, no debris. On a narrow bark ledge at that edge, very small in the frame and seen from behind, a few survivors stand close together: tiny carved hand-made stick-thin figures with large round heads and long thin twig limbs, not human proportions. Among them an elderly woman cook in an apron holding a long ladle bends over a small cooking pot with one small orange flame under it, its glow on their backs. Beside her one figure kneels at the bark wall, carving the first ring of a round door. Grey early light, umber, pale tan wood, one warm flame.
